claim.summary: Finite configuration, Fejer kernel K_L, off-line pairs gamma_j +- i delta_j of multiplicity m_j: (a) D_off(tau) >= - sum m_j e^{delta_j L} min(2L, 8/(L((tau - gamma_j)^2 + delta_j^2))), so if all delta_j <= theta and theta L >= 2 the density is at least -8 M e^{theta L}/(L theta^2); (b) with delta* the largest distance and tau off the heights and midpoints of the pairs at delta*, for every L_1 some L > L_1 has D_L(tau) <= -q' e^{delta* L}/L, q' < q = sum |c_j|^2/(2 sum |c_j|), c_j = m_j/(tau - gamma_j - i delta*)^2; hence D_L(tau) >= -C e^{theta L} for all large L forces delta* <= theta.
claim.assessment: Working proof: two elementary bounds for the kernel at complex arguments; the leading term at the largest distance is a real trigonometric polynomial in L with mean zero, whose negative part has mean at least q.

claim.summary: I(a) = (1/a) int_a^{2a} log|2 cos u| du >= -2 for every a > 0; hence for P(y) = prod_{i<=n} (1 + e^{-i y eta_i}), eta_i > 0 (nonnegative integer coefficients, sum M = 2^n) and every L_0 > 0, the mean of log|P| over [L_0, 2 L_0] is at least -2n and sup over that interval of |P|/M is at least M^{-1 - 2/log 2}.
claim.assessment: Working proof by counting the intervals where |2 cos| < 1 that [a, 2a] meets, each carrying the Clausen value Cl_2(pi/3) of the negative part.

claim.summary: Off-line pairs at one distance delta with heights in an interval of length c delta, c <= 1, b_0 = delta L_0 > 1, kappa > 1, Lambda* = (pi c/2)(b_0 - 1)(kappa b_0 - 1)/((kappa - 1) b_0) <= pi c kappa b_0/(2(kappa - 1)): sup over L in [L_0, kappa L_0] of sup_tau Re G_L is at least (pi^2/100)(e^{-1 - Lambda*} - 4 b_0 e^{-b_0})_+^2 M/delta^2, with no dependence on the number of pairs, gaps or multiplicities; against the factor e^{b_0} the exponent is positive exactly when c < (kappa - 1)/(pi kappa).
claim.assessment: Working proof: the one-sided Fourier relation at x = 1/delta for every length of the range bounds the cluster's sum on an interval, and the harmonic majorant inequality of the positive sum majorant, as v tends to 0, bounds how small it can be there.

claim.summary: In the setting of the one-sided density decomposition, with H_jl = 2/(2 delta + i(gamma_j - gamma_l))^3, J = int_0^inf x^2 e^{-2 delta x} |P(x - L)|^2 dx >= lambda_min(H) sum m_j^2 > 0, A1 = pi delta^2 J/M, eps = 2 pi L e^{-b} M and W the span of the heights: sup_tau Re G >= (A1/4 - eps/2)/(W + 16 M/A1); the lower bound for J does not depend on L, so no cluster makes the off-line part of the density nonnegative at arbitrarily large lengths.
claim.assessment: Working proof: Plancherel for G, nonnegativity of the integral of G^2, the integral of G by inversion, and the decay of G away from the heights. claim.summary: One-sided density with the Fejer kernel, off-line pairs at one distance delta with heights in an interval of length c delta, c <= 1, b = delta L > 1, 1/b < beta < 1 with log((1 - 1/b)/(1 - beta)) + (1 - beta)/(1 - 1/b) - 1 > pi c: sup Re G >= (pi^2/100)(e^{-beta b} - 4 b e^{-b})_+^2 M/delta^2, so some tau has D_off <= -(2M/(L delta^2))((pi^2/100) e^b (e^{-beta b} - 4 b e^{-b})_+^2 - 3); no dependence on the number of pairs, their gaps or their multiplicities.

claim.summary: One-sided density with the Fejer kernel: for k+1 off-line pairs at heights gamma_0 + j pi/L with multiplicities binom(k, j) at one distance delta, |G| <= (k+1)! (pi/b)^k/delta^2 and D_off >= -(2 e^b/(L delta^2)) (k+1)! (pi/b)^k - 6 * 2^k/(L delta^2); with real points on a lattice of spacing s <= 2 pi/L the whole density is nonnegative once 2 pi/s is at least that bound, which for k = floor(b/pi) is at most (2 e^2/(L delta^2)) (b/pi + 1)^(3/2) e^((1 - 1/pi) b) + 6 * 2^(b/pi)/(L delta^2).
claim.assessment: Working proof: the exponential sum is (1 + q)^k with |1 + q| <= pi x/L. With real density l/(2 pi), for each length with b up to about 1.47 log l (asymptotically) the cluster built for that length is hidden at it, where a single pair shows from about log l; its multiplicities are at most l^0.32 there. One cluster per length; not shown that a fixed cluster hides at shorter lengths, that the family shows soon after, or that no admissible cluster hides longer.
